To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

M-convolutions of densities of products and/or ratios of two statistically independently distributed real scalar or real or complex matrix variables can be considered as products and ratios of the corresponding Mellin convolutions.

Mellin convoluted products and ratios are related to products and ratios of independent positive random variables in both the scalar and matrix cases and to fractional calculus in both the scalar variable and the matrix cases.
M-convolutions of scalar and matrix-variate products and ratios can be used to describe products and ratios of independently distributed positive real or complex random variables.

a new type of convolution that can be applied to the analysis and synthesis of random variables, and also in applied analysis and in fractional calculus.
